Petite

/puh-TEET/ — rhymes with sweet · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Petite describes someone or something notably small and slight in size.

The petite dancer was often lifted highest in the routines.

Worked Example

The petite flutist had slender, graceful fingers perfect for the difficult passages, and the orchestra kept her front and center where she could be heard clearly.

Petite captures her small, slight build in a precise way — not just small, but elegantly so. The word has a note of grace that 'small' or 'tiny' would lack, and it suits her delicate artistry.

How Petite Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

small

small: below average in size, plain and general

diminutive

diminutive: notably small in a neat, charming way

tiny

tiny: very small, much smaller than usual

Antonyms

towering

towering: extremely tall and imposing in height

hulking

hulking: large, heavy, and powerfully built

How Strong Is It? — small → petite → diminutive → tiny

small vs. petite

small vs. petite: Small is a plainer, weaker word than petite: small just means below average in size, while petite adds a sense of dainty, graceful build.

diminutive vs. petite

diminutive vs. petite: Diminutive is a notch stronger than petite — a petite person is pleasantly small and slight, while diminutive draws real attention to just how little someone or something is.

tiny vs. petite

tiny vs. petite: Tiny is the strongest of the set, well beyond petite: a petite dancer is short and slight, but something tiny is dramatically, strikingly small.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — petit

Root — petit: small, little (French (Old French, 11th century))

Put it together

Put it together: Petite is simply the French word petit, 'small,' borrowed whole into English in its feminine form. English kept the French flavor, too: petite describes someone or something small in a trim, dainty, graceful way.

Use the root in a new word: petty

Use the root in a new word: petty: A petty complaint is a small, unimportant one — petty is just an older English spelling of the very same French petit, 'small,' behind petite.

Word Choice

formal / polite

Petite is the graceful term for someone small and delicate — common in fashion and dance, and it carries an accent of elegance. 'Small' is more neutral; 'tiny' is informal and blunt.
